turns.doctor_question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Hi. Well, I came in because... I guess I've been getting really stuck on some things lately. I work in production, and they recently had me start helping out with the safety trainings. But ever since I started doing that, I just can’t seem to stop noticing my hands. Like, when I’m pointing things out to the others, all I can focus on is how wrinkly and uneven my hands look. 

And then... well, it's my face, too. They took some photos of the trainings for the company newsletter, and looking at them, I just keep thinking my face looks crooked. I've pointed it out, but other people say they don’t see it at all. It's just really been bothering me, and I can't seem to let it go.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient describes persistent preoccupation with perceived flaws in physical appearance (wrinkly, uneven hands and a crooked face) that others do not observe.

turns.doctor_question: Are these thoughts about your hands and face affecting your work or relationships in any way?
turns.patient_response: Well, it hasn't stopped me from doing my job or anything like that. I still go to work and I still do the safety trainings. But... I guess I am a bit slower getting ready for work on the days I have to do the trainings, just trying to make sure I look okay. And, like I said about the newsletter, I've definitely started ducking out of the way when I see a camera. I even find myself hesitating a bit before going to some of the work get-togethers or social things that I used to just go to without thinking about it. It just makes me feel a little more self-conscious, I suppose.

turns.doctor_question: Do you find yourself repeating certain actions over and over, like checking your appearance in the mirror, as a way to deal with these thoughts about your hands and face?
turns.patient_response:
Well, yes, I suppose I do. Before I have to do a safety class, or even if I'm just heading to a senior-center workshop, I’ll go check the bathroom mirror a few times. I'll put lotion on my hands, and I kind of turn my face different ways in the light just to see how it looks. 

Sometimes I'll even ask a coworker if I look all right, just to be sure. Doing all that does make me run a little behind schedule sometimes, like I mentioned earlier, but... I still get myself there. I don't let it stop me from showing up.

symptom_reasoning.S068: The patient explicitly confirms engaging in repetitive behaviors in response to appearance concerns, including repeatedly checking the mirror, inspecting their face in the light, applying lotion, and seeking reassurance from coworkers.
